source.body:
## Question
What does Grok Bot require from a custom remote MCP server: transport, authentication, tool-schema limits, timeouts, and how tool calls show up in the chat?

## Steps
- Read xAI's Grok Bot documentation on MCP servers, skills, routines and approval rules.
- Stand up a hello-world Streamable HTTP MCP server behind a Cloudflare tunnel.
- Connect it from Grok Bot and call one tool.
- Find out how to export a chat for the bounty submission.

## Done when
- `docs/grok-bot.md` records the working connection steps, the auth scheme, limits found and the export method.
- If custom MCP is not possible, the doc records the fallback (a skill that calls our HTTP API from the Bot's terminal) and the agent issues are updated.

comments.author: jere67
comments.text:
Documentation half done in #39 (`docs/grok-bot.md`).

Findings:
- Grok Bot has no web client. It runs as a desktop app and a mobile app, so the hands-on test cannot be driven from a browser.
- Custom connectors accept a Remote HTTPS MCP server with a static HTTP header, so a bearer token is our auth scheme. No OAuth needed.
- Cloudflare quick tunnels work with Streamable HTTP and not with SSE.
- Routines can be started by a webhook call, which lets our backend wake the Bot on an onchain or market event.
- The docs show no whole-chat export. The sponsor needs to say which format the bounty accepts.

Still open: the six hands-on checks listed at the end of the doc. They need the desktop app, once the MCP server from #9 is up.

comments.author: jere67
comments.text: Correction (#41): Grok Bot does have a web client at grok.com/bot, with the same Connect Apps, Skills and Automations settings and the Add a custom connector dialog. The hands-on checks can be driven from the browser once the MCP server from #9 is running.

comments.author: jere67
comments.text:
## First live run from the Grok Bot web client (2026-11-15)

Connector `Mandate` added through Connect Apps -> Add a custom connector, pointing at the Cloudflare quick tunnel with an `Authorization: Bearer` header.

**Confirmed**

- [x] The connector lists all three tools (`get_setup_state`, `ping`, `whoami`) as enabled.
- [x] Grok Bot calls the tools from a plain chat request and shows each raw result in a "Text" block: the text summary followed by the structured JSON.
- [x] No Auto Review card appeared for any of the seven calls, so nothing needed "Always allow" for these read-only tools.
  This still has to be re-checked once a tool with side effects (`propose_trade`) exists.
- [x] Grok Bot reads the setup checklist (`actor` and `hint`) and tells the owner what to do next in its own words.
- [x] Each tool call is a fresh MCP session: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/call`, about 3 s apart.
  The stateless server design fits this.

**Found and fixed**

- The third call of the first run failed with a Cloudflare 502 that never reached the server.
  Cause and fix are in #48 (idle keep-alive shorter than the tunnel's connection reuse window).
  After the fix, four calls in a row succeeded.
- Grok Bot does not retry a failed call by itself; it reports the error and asks.
  The skill text (#12) should tell it to retry once after a transport error.

**Still open**

- [ ] Result size limit and tool timeout (needs a tool with a large or slow result).
- [ ] Auto Review behaviour for a write tool.
- [ ] Routine triggered by webhook (#40).
- [ ] Chat export method for the bounty submission.

comments.author: jere67
comments.text:
## Tool list is frozen when the connector is added (2026-11-15)

After the server went from 3 tools to 15 (#51), Grok Bot still saw only the original three.
The server log shows Grok Bot sends `initialize` and `tools/call` on each call and never asks for `tools/list` again; it listed the tools only when the connector was added.
The connector page has no refresh control, only Disconnect.

Consequences:
- After adding or renaming tools, the connector must be disconnected and added again (the owner pastes the header value again).
- Changes to an existing tool's behaviour or result shape are picked up immediately (Grok Bot noticed the new `status`, `reasons` and `nextAction` fields on `get_setup_state`).
- Changes to a tool's description or input schema are probably not picked up until reconnecting. To verify.
- Plan: reconnect once, after `buy_signal` (#21) lands, so the tool set is complete; and move to a stable address (#25) so the Server URL stops changing.

comments.author: jere67
comments.text:
## Finding: Grok Bot reads the tool list only when the connector is added

Observed on 2026-11-15 with the server at `8db836b` (16 tools).

- After the server went from 3 to 16 tools, Grok Bot and the connector page kept listing only `get_setup_state`, `ping`, `whoami`.
- Disconnecting and adding the connector again with the same URL did not refresh the list. At that time `tools/list` was 61,038 bytes (it included output schemas).
- Adding it again with a changed URL (`/mcp?v=2`, same server) while `tools/list` was 17,536 bytes (output schemas off, PR #53) gave all 16 tools.
- Two things changed between the failed and the working attempt (URL and list size), so the cause is not isolated: either xAI caches the list per URL, or it dropped the larger list.
- The connector page has no refresh control, only Disconnect.

What the server log shows when a connector is added: client `connectors-manager 0.1.0` sends `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list` (twice), and `grok-validator 0.1` sends `initialize`.
On a tool call it sends `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/call` and never `tools/list`, so a tool added later is invisible until the connector is added again.

Working rule for the demo:

1. Freeze the tool list before the final connector is added.
2. After any change to tool names or input schemas, add the connector again under a new query string (`?v=3`, ...).
3. Keep `MCP_ADVERTISE_OUTPUT_SCHEMAS` off.

## Live check with 16 tools

Prompt: count the tools, get the weekly BTC ladder, buy a signal for it.

- Grok Bot reported 16 tools.
- `get_ladder` returned in 1.6 s (3,920 bytes), `buy_signal` in 2.6 s (3,659 bytes), status `approved`.
- The signal cost 0.001 USDC and Grok Bot quoted the receipt id.
- No approval card was shown for `buy_signal`, although it is not a read-only tool.
- Its summary of cheap, fair and expensive strikes matched the signal's data.
